we propose to add two new developing components to addre ss concerns (i) and (ii): (PT1) the involvement of patients and patient advocacy groups at the development stage to identify and address trust-inhibiting treatment-restrictions in the AI;

Therefore, the envelopment needs to guarantee that the medical professional can appropriately oversee the employment of the AI and has the autonomy to override and/or eschew the use of the medical AI.
The latter part of the requirement prescribes the implementation of suitable transparent algorithms and precludes the use of opaque black box AI applications.

Therefore, in order to judge whether medical AI can be relied upon, medical professionals need to be mad e aware of the composition of the training data as well as any differences in the performances of the algorithm for different patient groups.

(PR1) the development of comprehensive, specific documentation for each medical AI that allows patients to understand how data is handled by the AI and which security risks to their data exist;
institutional routes need to be developed to preserve patients’ability to make decisions about their own treatment, including forgoing the use of medical AI all together.

unlisted_practices: Involve medical professionals in medical AI development, with a medical officer role holding far-reaching rights and veto power over AI development and responsible for implementing the envelopment framework.
Subject each medical AI to an independent institutional ethical assessment that draws on the fact sheet and medical officer reports.

Develop institutional guidelines for integrating each medical AI into the consultation and decision-making process that preserve shared decision-making and dialogue between patients and medical professionals.
Provide legally or institutionally binding safeguards with clearly signposted opportunities for patients to involve medical professionals at appropriate moments when using patient-accessible AI.
Ensure patient-accessible medical AI leads patients back onto recognized clinical pathways.
Use computational methods to make the intermediate steps of AI algorithms transparent during development.
